title: `ValueDataSource`'s equality arm compares an array comparand by REFERENCE — `{ tags: ['a','b'] }` excludes every row even when the stored array is deep-equal
body:
Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`) on behalf of the objectui#8447 dev, who measured it while landing PR #8512 and was locked out of both dedupe channels (`search_issues` rate-limited; repo-scoped REST 403). ⛔ Not claimed.

## The defect

`matchesFilter`'s simple-equality branch in `packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts` ends with:

```ts
} else {
  // Simple equality
  if (value !== condition) return false;
}
```

An array comparand takes this branch (the operator loop is guarded by `!Array.isArray(condition)`). `!==` on two arrays compares **references**, so `{ tags: ['a','b'] }` excludes every row — including rows whose stored `tags` is deep-equal to the comparand.

Silent, and fail-**closed**: the list comes back empty with no error and no warning.

## Why it is separate from objectui#8447

That card is about the operator switch's `default: break` arm — unknown operators adding **no** constraint and matching everything. This is the **equality** branch, and it fails in the opposite direction. PR #8512 deliberately did not touch it: same function, different arm, opposite sign.

⚠️ Note the interaction before fixing: the guard `!Array.isArray(condition)` is what routes an array comparand here in the first place. Whatever repair is chosen must not accidentally let an array comparand fall into the operator loop, where its **indices** would be read as operator names — the same shape `$not` had (`filter-converter.ts:229-232`).

## The decision in it

"Deep-equal" is not the only defensible reading of `{ tags: ['a','b'] }` against a stored array. It could reasonably mean set-equality, contains-all, or contains-any, and `@objectstack/spec` should be the authority rather than this adapter inventing one. Establish what the spec says (and what `$in` / `$contains` already mean for array-valued fields) before writing the comparison.

## ⭐ For whoever takes it

The caricature is deep-equality that returns **true** too readily — e.g. comparing `JSON.stringify` output, which makes `['a','b']` equal `['a','b']` but also makes key order and number formatting load-bearing. A pin asserting "the deep-equal row is now returned" passes for that too. The non-regression axis is the discriminating one: rows that should NOT match (different length, different order if order matters, a superset) must still be excluded, and every scalar equality case must be unchanged.

## Related

objectui#8447 / PR #8512 (the sibling arm of the same function) · objectui#7349

## Dedup

⚠️ **Declared, NOT claimed.** This repo's issue search returns false zeros: `search_issues` for `ValueDataSource` returns **0**, while objectui#8447's own title contains that word (and recency is not the cause — `InspectorSelectField` returns 3, including an issue filed later than #8447). A zero from this instrument is not evidence of absence. **No dedup claim is made.**
